source_refs.note: Exercise 5.1 (book p. 154), Question 4; answer key PDF 306 (Answers 5.1, no printed answer).

blocks.prompt: 4. Show that the medians of the triangle with vertices \(A(3, 2)\), \(B(-1, -5)\) and \(C(7, 2)\) are concurrent.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh 'show that' (saabit karo) wala sawal hai; is ka jawab koi number nahi, balke saboot hai. Book ki answer key mein is ka jawab nahi diya gaya, is liye hum poora saboot likhenge.
Pehle teeno medians ki equations nikalni hain, phir dikhana hai ke woh ek point par milte hain.
Hathiyar: Theorem 3, yani coefficients ka determinant zero hona chahiye.
Plan: mid-points, teen medians, determinant, aur aakhir mein common point nikal kar tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(3, 2)\), \(B(-1, -5)\), \(C(7, 2)\).
Saabit karna: medians \(AD\), \(BE\), \(CF\) concurrent hain.
Tareeqa: two-point form se medians, phir Theorem 3 ka determinant.
Socho: hum teen lines ke baare mein dawa kar rahe hain ke woh ek point par milti hain. Is dawe ka saboot do tarah se diya ja sakta hai: determinant se, ya point nikal kar teeno mein rakh kar. Hum pehla tareeqa saboot ke liye aur doosra tasdeeq ke liye istemal karenge.

Mid-points
\[D\left(\dfrac{-1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{-5 + 2}{2}\right) = D\left(3, -\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
\[E\left(\dfrac{3 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 2}{2}\right) = E(5, 2)\]
\[F\left(\dfrac{3 - 1}{2}, \dfrac{2 - 5}{2}\right) = F\left(1, -\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: \(D\), \(E\), \(F\) sides \(BC\), \(CA\), \(AB\) ke mid-points hain; har median vertex se samne wali side ke mid-point tak jata hai.

Median \(AD\)
\(A(3, 2)\) aur \(D\left(3, -\frac{3}{2}\right)\) dono ka \(x\) barabar hai, to
\[x = 3 \;\text{ or }\; x - 3 = 0 \;\ldots(i)\]
Kyun: yeh vertical line hai. Two-point form mein \(x_2 - x_1 = 0\) denominator mein aa jata, is liye seedha \(x = 3\) likha.
Dhyan dein: is line ke coefficients \(a = 1\), \(b = 0\), \(c = -3\) hain; determinant mein \(b = 0\) likhna na bhoolein.

Median \(BE\)
\[\dfrac{y + 5}{2 + 5} = \dfrac{x + 1}{5 + 1}\]
\[6(y + 5) = 7(x + 1)\]
\[7x - 6y - 23 = 0 \;\ldots(ii)\]
Kyun: \(B(-1, -5)\) aur \(E(5, 2)\) se two-point form; cross-multiply kar ke \(6y + 30 = 7x + 7\).

Median \(CF\)
\[\dfrac{y - 2}{-\frac{3}{2} - 2} = \dfrac{x - 7}{1 - 7}\]
\[-6(y - 2) = -\tfrac{7}{2}(x - 7)\]
\[12y - 24 = 7x - 49\]
\[7x - 12y - 25 = 0 \;\ldots(iii)\]
Kyun: \(C(7, 2)\) aur \(F\left(1, -\frac{3}{2}\right)\) se two-point form. \(-\frac{3}{2} - 2 = -\frac{7}{2}\). Dono taraf \(-2\) se multiply kiya to fraction khatam.

Theorem 3 lagayein
\[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 7 & -6 & -23 \\ 7 & -12 & -25 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(150 - 276) - 0 - 3(-84 + 42)\]
\[= -126 + 126 = 0\]
Kyun: har row ek median ke coefficients \((a, b, c)\) hain. Pehli row ke saath expand kiya; beech wala term \(0\) ki wajah se khatam. Determinant zero hai aur koi do medians parallel nahi, is liye medians concurrent hain.
Dhyan dein: determinant ki pehli row \((1, 0, -3)\) hai, kyunke \(x - 3 = 0\) mein \(y\) ka coefficient zero hai. Zero wali entry expansion ko aasaan bana deti hai; is liye pehli row ke saath expand karna faidemand tha.

Tasdeeq: common point
(i) se \(x = 3\); (ii) mein: \(21 - 6y - 23 = 0\), yani \(y = -\frac{1}{3}\). Ab (iii) mein:
\[7(3) - 12\left(-\tfrac{1}{3}\right) - 25 = 21 + 4 - 25 = 0\]
Yeh centroid hai: \(\left(\frac{3 - 1 + 7}{3}, \frac{2 - 5 + 2}{3}\right) = \left(3, -\frac{1}{3}\right)\). Saboot bilkul pakka.
Yeh point centroid hai, aur centroid hamesha teeno medians par hota hai; is liye yeh tasdeeq saboot ko aur pakka kar deti hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: medians \(x - 3 = 0\), \(7x - 6y - 23 = 0\), \(7x - 12y - 25 = 0\) concurrent hain (determinant \(= 0\)); woh \(\left(3, -\frac{1}{3}\right)\) par milte hain.
